codex.text: The design burns its own evidence: using the sealed holdout as the adoption arbiter contaminates it — once this gate's result selects or rejects the challenger, the holdout is spent, and any future challengers compared on the same window inherit selection bias. "Reduces false-positive trades" is unmeasurable as stated (there's no ground-truth label for a "false positive" entry), and since hysteresis mechanically shrinks trade count, both the expectancy improvement and the 10%-drawdown allowance are noise-dominated at small n with no minimum-sample, bootstrap, or significance requirement. The free parameters — two consecutive observations, 10% drawdown tolerance — appear asserted rather than swept, and there's no walk-forward or multi-regime check, so a single-window pass is indistinguishable from regime luck. Finally, the proposal omits required governance: no ExperimentRegistry entry specified, no commitment to promotion solely via `bot/scripts/research_promote_champion.py` after all `promote.py` gates, and "net of spread and slippage" names no cost model — whose assumptions govern the arithmetic.

Two observations may merely delay entries and reduce trade count, making expectancy appear better through selection bias without testing statistical significance or regime stability. “Validated-state” is undefined, inviting label leakage or post hoc tuning; the proposal also lacks walk-forward validation and a minimum trade-count threshold. The 10% drawdown limit is arbitrary and ignores tail loss, exposure concentration, and uncertainty around holdout results.

hermes.text: The 1–5% flip thresholds are arbitrary and ignore whether flipped labels cluster in high-impact regimes, so a low aggregate rate could still materially bias validation. “Explicit MT5 server-time alignment” is underspecified without an independently verified server-time source and DST/weekend rules, making the comparison potentially circular. Recomputing labels from existing logs may not recover the original raw timestamp semantics, so the proposal needs an immutable raw-deal sample and a holdout validation before claiming the patch hardens telemetry.

The A/B recomputation is not decisive: “explicit MT5 server-time alignment” is treated as ground truth without proving the broker’s timezone, DST rules, rollover semantics, or clock synchronization from authoritative raw data. The 5%/1% flip thresholds are arbitrary, ignore class imbalance and economic impact, and invite overfitting to a single 90-day window; no out-of-sample, instrument/session stratification, or independent replay validation is specified. It also underestimates safety risk by proposing altered ingest semantics without defining immutable raw inputs, provenance, registry failure handling, or proving that validated-state decisions cannot change during measurement.

opencode.text: The fatal flaw is deciding directly on the sealed holdout: setting thresholds (60% confidence, +10% expectancy, −30% trade count) and iterating until they pass converts a one-shot holdout into a tuning set, leaving nothing clean to confirm the winner, and the proposal pre-commits to no one-query limit, no ExperimentRegistry entry, and no pre-registration of criteria before unlocking. Its central claim is unmeasurable as written — "positive net expected value after modeled spread and slippage" inherits whatever cost assumptions are fed in, with no reconciliation to realized demo fills, and a "≥10%" expectancy delta is asserted with no sample size, confidence interval, or multiple-testing correction despite an obvious family-of-variants search. The comparison design is also confounded: allowing up to 30% fewer trades changes regime exposure, so improved expectancy with flat max drawdown can come purely from dodging an unfavorable stretch of the holdout window; require exposure-normalized, risk-adjusted stats computed across sub-periods (walk-forward), not single-window point estimates. Finally, "advance it" must route through every gate in bot/aegis/research/promote.py rather than this bespoke criterion, and rejection-vs-promotion outcomes must be recorded either way — the proposal is silent on both governance paths.

The 60% analogue-confidence threshold and 10% expectancy-improvement cutoff are arbitrary and may be tuned to the sealed holdout, creating overfitting and invalidating its independence. “Modeled” spread/slippage and “net expectancy” are not defined or required to be calibrated against realized execution costs, while maximum drawdown and trade-count changes lack statistical uncertainty, minimum sample size, and regime-wise validation. The proposal also omits robustness checks, multiple-testing controls, and explicit confirmation that promotion proceeds only through the governed champion-promotion gates.

proposals.text: Candidate: audit the validated-state gate's short-horizon labels for broker-server timestamp misalignment before any new strategy work. Hypothesis: since the recent demo deal-watermark timezone shift, a measurable fraction of outcome labels for deals spanning the daily server rollover (or weekend gap) are computed on windows offset by 2–3 hours, systematically inflating apparent win rate and feeding the validated-state gate biased features. Falsification test: recompute ~90 days of outcome_log entries twice — once as currently ingested, once with explicit MT5 server-time alignment at ingest — and diff the label classifications; if ≥5% of labels flip class, the misalignment is material and timestamp normalization becomes the next challenger experiment (registered in ExperimentRegistry, gated through promote.py like any other); if <1% flip, the watermark patch was sufficient and this candidate is rejected on record. Either outcome is decisive within one research cycle using existing data, requires no code changes to the runner or champion during measurement, and directly hardens the "truthful short-horizon telemetry" foundation every downstream gate depends on.

Test a stricter validated-state entry filter requiring positive net expected value after modeled spread and slippage plus a minimum 60% analogue outcome confidence. Evaluate it on the sealed holdout against the current gate, keeping position sizing and all other execution rules unchanged. Advance it only if net expectancy improves by at least 10% without increasing maximum drawdown or reducing trade count by more than 30%; otherwise reject and retain the current gate.

Test a research-only hysteresis gate requiring two consecutive validated-state observations before entry, hypothesizing that it reduces false-positive trades. Evaluate it against the current gate on a sealed holdout, net of spread and slippage, using expectancy, drawdown, and trade count. Adopt it only if expectancy improves with no more than a 10% increase in drawdown; otherwise reject it.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.

codex.text: Test a research-only hysteresis gate whose “validated state” is defined ex ante from information available at decision time, with entry false positives labeled as trades that fail a preregistered net-of-cost outcome threshold over a fixed horizon. Register the experiment before execution, sweep observation counts and drawdown tolerances only within development data, and compare the current and challenger gates through multi-regime walk-forward validation using the runner’s documented spread/slippage model. Require a minimum trade count plus bootstrap confidence intervals for expectancy, maximum drawdown, tail loss, exposure concentration, and trade count; use the sealed holdout exactly once for confirmation, never as the selection or adoption arbiter. Promote only if the preregistered economic and robustness criteria pass, including improved expectancy with uncertainty consistent with improvement and no material deterioration in risk, and only through `bot/scripts/research_promote_champion.py` after every `promote.py` gate passes; otherwise retain the challenger as rejected research.

hermes.text: Candidate: before any new strategy work, run a read-only audit of the validated-state gate's short-horizon labels for broker-server timestamp misalignment since the demo deal-watermark timezone shift. Ground truth will be established non-circularly by freezing an immutable raw-deal sample at ingest (original timestamps plus provenance hashes) and cross-checking it against an independently observed broker clock (terminal/tick server time sampled live across sessions), with the broker's timezone, DST behavior, and daily-rollover semantics documented in the ExperimentRegistry entry before any comparison. Materiality is judged by stratified economic impact, not one aggregate number: label classifications are recomputed both ways and diffed per instrument, per session (Asia/London/NY), and within ±3h of rollover and weekend gaps, flagging only if flips concentrate in regimes that sit near the gate's decision boundary or carry outsized P&L weight. Calibration runs on one 90-day window with an untouched out-of-sample holdout confirming flip-rate stability, plus a replay check verifying recomputed labels reproduce from raw deals alone. During measurement nothing changes: ingest semantics, champion, and validated-state outputs stay frozen (provenance-tagged so any drift is detectable), and any registry or ground-truth failure records honestly and stops the experiment. Only if stratified impact is confirmed does server-time normalization proceed as a challenger through promote.py like any other candidate; a clean result rejects this on record with the frozen sample retained as evidence the watermark patch sufficed.

opencode.text: Pre-register one fixed candidate filter, cost model, minimum sample size, statistical tests, and promotion criteria in `ExperimentRegistry` before a single sealed-holdout query; do not tune thresholds after unlock. Calibrate modeled spread and slippage against realized MT5 DEMO fills, and evaluate net, exposure-normalized risk-adjusted performance with confidence intervals and multiple-testing controls across pre-defined walk-forward sub-periods. Compare equivalent exposure and regime coverage against the current gate, reporting expectancy, drawdown, trade count, and uncertainty rather than relying on point thresholds alone. Record both acceptance and rejection outcomes, preserve rejected challengers, and permit promotion only if all gates in `bot/aegis/research/promote.py` pass.
